new_jobs.title: Reading Program Coordinator, Alpha - $120,000/year USD
new_jobs.description:
$120,000/year salary, paid weekly, with health, dental, and vision coverage starting on day one
On-site at a single Alpha campus: Beverly Hills, La Jolla (San Diego), Malibu, Palo Alto, Piedmont, San Francisco, or Santa Monica, CA; Greenwich, CT; Boston, MA; New York City, NY; or Seattle, WA (relocation assistance available)
Full-time 40 hours/week, 100% in-classroom instruction with K-3 students

Your structured-literacy credential — whether Orton-Gillingham, LETRS, Wilson, IMSE, or a Master's in reading instruction — has opened the door to every K-3 reading position you've pursued. In most of those roles, it also became your ceiling: you delivered someone else's program and reported outcomes. Here, that credential is your starting point. If this difference resonates with you, read on.

Alpha has redesigned traditional instruction. Students progress through academic content independently using AI-adaptive applications. There are no lectures, no textbooks, no pacing guides. Your role occupies the space where human expertise remains essential. You create 20-minute small-group workshops based on real-time app data; sessions are brief by design, because precision is more effective than duration. You also lead motivation sessions that ensure 100% of your students reach their weekly app targets using Alpha's motivational framework (school currency, leaderboards, age-appropriate gamification). When you catch a student's miscue during a session, you identify the phonemic gap and have the next day's workshop revised before the end of the day. That is the expectation.

Families at these campuses have selected Alpha for results, not simply for enrollment. Parents receive weekly data on their child's reading progress and they engage actively. You will field specific questions about individual student advancement, and "they're doing fine" will not suffice. You will need to reference the running record, identify the phonemic gap, and describe your intervention. That level of accountability should energize you, not burden you.

Your initial months focus on establishing credibility. Workshops must be engaging, appropriately leveled, and demonstrably effective; student satisfaction and "love your Guide" survey scores (target 90%+) measure this directly. Once you establish yourself, your influence expands beyond your classroom: strategies that succeed with your students become models for other Alpha campuses to implement, and your diagnostic precision informs how reading is taught as Alpha scales. The work you do here extends beyond your immediate environment.

Prior to hiring, you will submit a short video in which you tell an engaging story for young children, and you will spend a full day on campus working directly with K-3 students. Low energy with children will disqualify you, regardless of your credentials. This is intentional. Apply today.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating small-group K-3 reading workshops using live adaptive-app data, anchored in structured-literacy approaches (Orton-Gillingham, Wilson, LETRS, IMSE, or equivalent)
Leading daily motivation sessions that drive 100% of your students to meet their weekly app goals through Alpha's motivational model (school currency, leaderboards, age-appropriate gamification)
Analyzing AI-generated performance data (fluency curves, decoding accuracy, comprehension signals) to modify instruction mid-day, not only during planning time
Conducting running records, fluency probes, and decoding assessments to generate gains that appear in the weekly campus data review
Serving as the energetic, relatable adult that your K-3 students are excited to see each day

What You Won’t Be Doing

Implementing a published reading curriculum, scripted program, or district pacing guide; you create lessons based on student data
Delivering lectures to a full classroom; all instruction occurs in small, targeted groups and students complete academic subjects through adaptive apps
Serving as a reading consultant, teacher coach, or district-level specialist; you are in the classroom with students daily
Managing a traditional classroom schedule: subject-by-subject lectures, homework review, test preparation. Your scheduled blocks consist of workshops, motivation sessions, and data-driven small groups
Drafting IEPs, 504 plans, or formal diagnostic reports; student progress is tracked through app data and your running records, not special-education documentation

Reading Program Coordinator Key Responsibilities

Generate measurable K-3 reading growth across phonics, fluency, and comprehension within a campus community where outcomes are reviewed weekly.

Basic Requirements

Structured-literacy certification (Orton-Gillingham, LETRS, Wilson Reading System, IMSE, CERI, Neuhaus, UFLI, or equivalent) OR a Master's degree in reading instruction
Bachelor's degree in any field, plus 2+ years of full-time K-3 structured reading instruction in a school or clinical setting within the last 5 years, using systematic phonics or structured literacy
Proven ability to design your own reading lessons and clearly explain what you teach and how, without depending on a published program
Willingness to work in person full-time at one Alpha campus: Beverly Hills, La Jolla (San Diego), Malibu, Palo Alto, Piedmont, San Francisco, or Santa Monica, CA; Greenwich, CT; Boston, MA; New York City, NY; or Seattle, WA (relocation support provided)
Willingness to work with all K-3 students (not exclusively struggling readers) and incorporate AI and adaptive-learning tools into daily instruction as those tools develop
Legal authorization to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Direct experience with AI-powered or adaptive reading platforms (e.g., Amira, Lexia, i-Ready, Reading Plus) for instructional planning or student data analysis
Documented record of measurable reading outcomes (fluency gains in WCPM, accuracy improvement, decoding level advancement) you can quantify
Familiarity with diagnostic reading assessments (DRA, DIBELS, AIMSweb) for creating differentiated groups
Experience in high-accountability school settings (independent, elite charter, premium tutoring with families who closely monitor outcomes)
Background in performance, youth sports coaching, or otherwise engaging a K-3 audience outside the reading classroom

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time (40 hours per week), long-term position. The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $60 USD/hour, which equates to $120,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

Compensation And Benefits

Student enrollment exceeds 900 students across all programs. The School has strong community partnerships, which enable it to provide practical experience to students.

For more information regarding the School of Public Health, click here.

Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.

Compensation And Benefits

Our benefits are a significant part of total compensation. Learn more at the SDSU Benefits Overview.

SDSU Values

At SDSU, our diversity gives us power and benefits every single member of our community. We encourage all members of our community to purposefully learn from one another through open and respectful dialogue and responsible engagement. At San Diego State University, we are a community of diverse individuals who have and represent many perspectives, beliefs, and identities. This diversity lends our community strength, and we commit to creating and sustaining an inclusive and intellectually vibrant environment that benefits all members of our university.

Consistent with California law and federal civil rights laws, San Diego State University (SDSU) provides equal opportunity in education and employment without unlawful discrimination or preferential treatment based on race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin. Our commitment to equal opportunity means ensuring that every student and employee has access to the resources and support they need to thrive and succeed in a university environment and in their communities. I, Section 31 of the California Constitution), other applicable state and federal anti-discrimination laws, and CSU’s Nondiscrimination Policy. new_jobs.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring two Voluntary Cleanup Program Site Managers (Hydrogeologist 3)
within the Toxics Cleanup Program (TCP) .

Location:

Southwest Region Office in Lacey, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
A minimum of one day every other week is required in the office.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by August 10, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

Join a mission-driven team working to protect Washington’s communities by advancing cleanup of sites impacted by hazardous substances released to the environment. As a Site Manager in the Toxics Cleanup Program's southwest region, you will manage cleanup projects that enroll in the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP), ensuring cleanups meet the requirements of the Model Toxics Control Act (MTCA). You will evaluate complex geologic and environmental data, guide consultants and property owners toward technically sound cleanup actions, and help move contaminated sites to closure. If you are energized by applying geologic expertise to real-world cleanup projects, and want to make a direct and positive impact across the region, we would be thrilled to welcome your talent to our team.

What You Will Do

Review and evaluate technical reports, sampling data, work plans, scopes of work, and corrective-action proposals to identify regulatory compliance, data adequacy, and next steps for contaminated sites.
Conduct and document initial investigations and site hazard assessments, including data analysis, contamination evaluation, and preparation of clear written recommendations and assessment reports.
Provide technical oversight and geologic/hydrogeologic review of complex cleanup sites, including evaluating field activities, monitoring-well installation, and environmental sampling plans.
Prepare technical correspondence, opinion letters, regulatory determinations, and other cleanup documentation that clearly communicates requirements and supports cleanup progress.
Collaborate with property owners, consultants, community members, and local or state agencies to address technical issues, communicate expectations, and support productive, solution-focused interactions.
Offer technical assistance and mentorship to junior staff, contribute to peer reviews, and participate in program workgroups, planning efforts, and policy review as needed.
Maintain accurate site records and ensure timely data submittals and document uploads in agency databases to support tracking, reporting, and regulatory decision-making.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Possession
of a valid Washington State Geologist license and Hydrogeologist Specialty license AND

Seven years of experience
as a hydrogeologist, hydrologist, geologist or closely allied profession. Experience must include the following:

Regulatory and Cleanup Oversight: Experience reviewing environmental cleanup investigations and applying state cleanup regulations to support compliance and sound regulatory decisions.
Environmental Project Management: Skill in managing multiple contaminated-site projects, coordinating work plans and schedules, and ensuring steady progress toward cleanup completion.
Geologic and Environmental Data Interpretation: Ability to interpret geologic, hydrogeologic, and environmental data to evaluate site conditions and confirm that investigations are sufficient for decision-making.
Technical Communication and Documentation: Strong technical writing skills, including preparing clear, defensible reports, letters, and regulatory determinations.
Collaboration and Issue Resolution: Effective at working collaboratively with property owners, consultants, local governments, community members, and internal teams to resolve project issues.
Quality Assurance and Field Oversight: Experience evaluating field investigation activities, sampling plans, and data-quality practices, and maintaining accurate site records.
Technical Leadership and Mentorship: Ability to mentor junior staff and contribute to team consistency through peer review and knowledge-sharing.

Education:

major study in hydrogeology, hydrology, geology or closely allied field.

Examples of how to qualify -- a valid Washington State Geologist license and:

7 years of experience.
6 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
5 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
4 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
3 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
1 year of experience AND a Master’s degree.
A Ph.D.

Special Requirements/Conditions Of Employment

Possession of a Washington State Geologist license.

NOTE:
Individuals who are interested in applying to this position, and believe they meet licensing requirements for the State of Washington based on reciprocity, are responsible for ensuring they meet licensing requirements for the State of Washington prior to submitting their application materials. These requirements can be found at the following website: WA State Licensing (DOL) Official Site: How to get your license: Geologists, engineering geologists, or hydrogeologists by reciprocity .

Desired Qualifications

Washington State Hydrogeologist Specialty License (or ability to obtain).
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training with current 8-hour refresher.
Advanced Environmental and Regulatory Interpretation: Demonstrated ability to analyze complex environmental, geologic, and regulatory information to develop clear, well-supported cleanup recommendations consistent with Model Toxics Control Act (MTCA), Underground Storage Tank (UST) regulations, and related environmental laws.
Technical Communication and Engagement Skills: Strong ability to convey complex technical and regulatory concepts clearly in writing and verbally to support understanding, navigate challenging interactions, and guide cleanup progress.
Collaborative Problem Solving and Relationship Building: Experience working constructively with property owners, consultants, local governments, and agency staff to identify and resolve sensitive or complicated technical issues.
Senior-Level Technical Leadership: Experience providing technical guidance, peer review, or mentorship that strengthens team capability and supports consistent, science-based cleanup decisions.
Applied Cleanup Project and Technical Tools Experience: Proficiency managing contaminated site cleanup projects and using relevant software tools (e.g., Visio, Adobe applications, statistical tools, groundwater modeling platforms) to enhance the clarity, efficiency, and defensibility of technical evaluations.

If you are excited about this role and meet the required qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Desired qualifications reflect additional knowledge, skills, or experience that are nice to have but not required. Studies have shown that some applicants, especially women and people of color, are less likely to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. At the Department of Ecology, we are dedicated to building a diverse and authentic workplace centered in belonging, and we welcome applicants with varied backgrounds and unique perspectives.

Supplemental Information

Our Commitment to DEIR

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR)
are core values central to Ecology's work. We strive to be a workplace where we are esteemed for sharing our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals and collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations.

Diversity:
We celebrate and appreciate diversity; our unique perspectives and abilities enrich us all and lead to innovative approaches and solutions.

Equity:
We champion equity, recognizing that each of us need different things to thrive.

Inclusion:
We intentionally create and hold space so that we all have meaningful opportunities to participate and contribute to Ecology’s work.

Respect:

We believe that DEIR is both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Qualified job seekers from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

The state may verify this information, and any false or misleading answers may result in rejection of your application or dismissal if employed.

Need an Accommodation?

Please contact us at 360-407-6186 or careers@ecy.wa.gov
If you are deaf or hard of hearing, you may call through the Washington Relay Service by dialing 711 or 1-800-833-6384.

Questions?

For specific questions about the position location options, schedule, or duties, please contact Marian Abbett at Marian.Abbett@ecy.wa.gov .
If you need assistance applying for this job, are inquiring about the status of your application, would like to request the full position description, or have any other questions, please contact the Recruitment Team at careers@ecy.wa.gov

About The Toxics Cleanup Program

The mission of the Toxics Cleanup Program (TCP) is to protect human health and the environment for the people of Washington by preventing, reducing, or eliminating exposure to contamination to support the development of environmentally and economically sustainable communities.

new_jobs.title: Reading Program Coordinator, Alpha - $120,000/year USD
new_jobs.description:
$120,000/year salary, paid weekly, with health, dental, and vision coverage starting on day one
On-site at a single Alpha campus: Beverly Hills, La Jolla (San Diego), Malibu, Palo Alto, Piedmont, San Francisco, or Santa Monica, CA; Greenwich, CT; Boston, MA; New York City, NY; or Seattle, WA (relocation assistance available)
Full-time 40 hours/week, 100% in-classroom instruction with K-3 students

Your structured-literacy credential — whether Orton-Gillingham, LETRS, Wilson, IMSE, or a Master's in reading instruction — has opened the door to every K-3 reading position you've pursued. In most of those roles, it also became your ceiling: you delivered someone else's program and reported outcomes. Here, that credential is your starting point. If this difference resonates with you, read on.

Alpha has redesigned traditional instruction. Students progress through academic content independently using AI-adaptive applications. There are no lectures, no textbooks, no pacing guides. Your role occupies the space where human expertise remains essential. You create 20-minute small-group workshops based on real-time app data; sessions are brief by design, because precision is more effective than duration. You also lead motivation sessions that ensure 100% of your students reach their weekly app targets using Alpha's motivational framework (school currency, leaderboards, age-appropriate gamification). When you catch a student's miscue during a session, you identify the phonemic gap and have the next day's workshop revised before the end of the day. That is the expectation.

Families at these campuses have selected Alpha for results, not simply for enrollment. Parents receive weekly data on their child's reading progress and they engage actively. You will field specific questions about individual student advancement, and "they're doing fine" will not suffice. You will need to reference the running record, identify the phonemic gap, and describe your intervention. That level of accountability should energize you, not burden you.

Your initial months focus on establishing credibility. Workshops must be engaging, appropriately leveled, and demonstrably effective; student satisfaction and "love your Guide" survey scores (target 90%+) measure this directly. Once you establish yourself, your influence expands beyond your classroom: strategies that succeed with your students become models for other Alpha campuses to implement, and your diagnostic precision informs how reading is taught as Alpha scales. The work you do here extends beyond your immediate environment.

Prior to hiring, you will submit a short video in which you tell an engaging story for young children, and you will spend a full day on campus working directly with K-3 students. Low energy with children will disqualify you, regardless of your credentials. This is intentional. Apply today.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating small-group K-3 reading workshops using live adaptive-app data, anchored in structured-literacy approaches (Orton-Gillingham, Wilson, LETRS, IMSE, or equivalent)
Leading daily motivation sessions that drive 100% of your students to meet their weekly app goals through Alpha's motivational model (school currency, leaderboards, age-appropriate gamification)
Analyzing AI-generated performance data (fluency curves, decoding accuracy, comprehension signals) to modify instruction mid-day, not only during planning time
Conducting running records, fluency probes, and decoding assessments to generate gains that appear in the weekly campus data review
Serving as the energetic, relatable adult that your K-3 students are excited to see each day

What You Won’t Be Doing

Implementing a published reading curriculum, scripted program, or district pacing guide; you create lessons based on student data
Delivering lectures to a full classroom; all instruction occurs in small, targeted groups and students complete academic subjects through adaptive apps
Serving as a reading consultant, teacher coach, or district-level specialist; you are in the classroom with students daily
Managing a traditional classroom schedule: subject-by-subject lectures, homework review, test preparation. Your scheduled blocks consist of workshops, motivation sessions, and data-driven small groups
Drafting IEPs, 504 plans, or formal diagnostic reports; student progress is tracked through app data and your running records, not special-education documentation

Reading Program Coordinator Key Responsibilities

Generate measurable K-3 reading growth across phonics, fluency, and comprehension within a campus community where outcomes are reviewed weekly.

Basic Requirements

Structured-literacy certification (Orton-Gillingham, LETRS, Wilson Reading System, IMSE, CERI, Neuhaus, UFLI, or equivalent) OR a Master's degree in reading instruction
Bachelor's degree in any field, plus 2+ years of full-time K-3 structured reading instruction in a school or clinical setting within the last 5 years, using systematic phonics or structured literacy
Proven ability to design your own reading lessons and clearly explain what you teach and how, without depending on a published program
Willingness to work in person full-time at one Alpha campus: Beverly Hills, La Jolla (San Diego), Malibu, Palo Alto, Piedmont, San Francisco, or Santa Monica, CA; Greenwich, CT; Boston, MA; New York City, NY; or Seattle, WA (relocation support provided)
Willingness to work with all K-3 students (not exclusively struggling readers) and incorporate AI and adaptive-learning tools into daily instruction as those tools develop
Legal authorization to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Direct experience with AI-powered or adaptive reading platforms (e.g., Amira, Lexia, i-Ready, Reading Plus) for instructional planning or student data analysis
Documented record of measurable reading outcomes (fluency gains in WCPM, accuracy improvement, decoding level advancement) you can quantify
Familiarity with diagnostic reading assessments (DRA, DIBELS, AIMSweb) for creating differentiated groups
Experience in high-accountability school settings (independent, elite charter, premium tutoring with families who closely monitor outcomes)
Background in performance, youth sports coaching, or otherwise engaging a K-3 audience outside the reading classroom

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

This announcement is open to United States Citizens; U.S. Nationals; and Career transition eligibles (CTAP, ICTAP, RPL).

Duties

Help

These positions are located within the Department of the Interior, U.S. Geological Survey, Geology, Geophysics, and Geochemistry Science Center, duty stationed in Lakewood, Colorado.

At the full performance level (GS-07)
the major duties of this position include, but are not limited to the following:

Conduct field phases of geologic data collection projects.
Calibrate, install, and maintain field instrument sites for monitoring magnetotellurics, seismicity, gravity, multi-spectral or hyperspectral remote sensing, and similar parameters.
Prepare rock samples for geochemical (e.g., trace metal or isotope) or physical (e.g., thin section or mineral separation) analyses.
Process and plot data using standard or specially developed computer software, including GIS software.
Assist scientists during the office phase of scientific projects including permitting, data management, and preparation of data for publication and release.

Pre-employment Medical Examination

This position involves field work where the duties of the position may involve arduous conditions and those involving on-site emergency response. Therefore you will be required to pass a pre-employment medical examination to ensure you can perform the essential duties and responsibilities of the position, with or without accommodation.

Work Environment

Most work takes place in an office or laboratory settings with adequate heat, light, and ventilation Office conditions do not require special safety precautions. Field conditions may include extreme heat or cold, rain or snow, and hazardous conditions such as exposure to extreme temperature, noxious or toxic gasses, ice or flooding.

Field work may occasionally also involve encounters with snakes, bears, and other wilderness dangers International field work may be conducted in culturally hostile areas.

Physical Demands

Some work of the position takes place mostly in an office or laboratory setting. No special physical effort is required. During emergency response periods, training of personnel on new equipment, or field work, the scientist may be expected to hike distances of several kilometers over uneven terrain while carrying equipment. Field work may require the use of proper personal protective gear, working in dusty, hot, humid, and extreme cold environments, occasional off-road driving of 4-wheel drive vehicles, traveling to remote field sites in helicopters or small fixed wing planes, and/or boats, lifting of equipment and objects weighing up to 20 kilograms may be necessary.

Driver's License

You will be required to maintain a valid State issued Driver's License as a condition of employment.

Travel

You will be required to travel for training, meetings or site visits (which will include field work).

Telework

You may be allowed to telework but only on a situational basis at management discretion.

RUIZ Engineering is seeking a GIS Technician to support active natural gas distribution, natural gas transmission, electric distribution, and preliminary engineering programs across multiple utility clients. This is a production-focused role that owns the full data lifecycle on assigned projects: setting up new projects in Survey123 and Field Maps, maintaining project boundaries and metadata, running QA/QC against field documentation, correcting geometry and connectivity errors, and delivering finished data packages to client GIS teams for final review and acceptance.

The technician also supports survey and CAD design workflows by processing Trimble Business Center data into usable formats for designers and loading preliminary data into ArcGIS Online for dashboard visibility. Success in this role requires precision, consistency, and the ability to manage several concurrent projects at different stages of the delivery cycle.

Key Responsibilities

Project Setup & Configuration

Set up new projects across active programs, including Survey123 form deployment, Field Maps configuration, project information, and boundary/limits definition
Configure and maintain field data collection applications to ensure inspection and construction crews capture complete and accurately attributed data
Update existing project configurations as scope, client requirements, or data standards change

QA/QC & Data Correction

Perform QA/QC of GIS data against service record cards, Survey123 field reports, and contractor as-built documentation submitted to the approved project folders
Identify and correct geometry and connectivity errors, including unsnapped points and lines, misaligned features, and incomplete or inconsistent attribution
Reconcile discrepancies between field-collected data, as-built documentation, and existing client GIS records

Client Deliverables & Submissions

Prepare and transmit final project submissions to client GIS groups for review and acceptance
Produce recurring client deliverables on schedule, including weekly distribution main exports to the client GIS team
Manage correction cycles on submissions returned by the client, applying revisions to GIS data or coordinating updated as-built documentation with field supervision, and resubmitting for approval

Survey & Preliminary Engineering Support

Process and pull Trimble Business Center (TBC) data to the server in DWG, DXF, SHP, and GDB formats for CAD designers
Load TBC geodatabase exports into ArcGIS Online and publish to web maps for preliminary dashboard visibility
Append TBC survey data into project GIS data where required, ensuring the correct feature definition (FXL) file is applied during processing
Export field-collected data from ArcGIS Pro to the server for designer use
Track survey crew locate work through the project management system and follow assignments through completion

Dashboards & Reporting

Build and maintain ArcGIS Online dashboards providing project status and progress visibility to internal teams and clients
Maintain the operator qualification (OQ) dashboard, uploading records as they are submitted by field operations and administrative staff
Ensure dashboards reflect current project data and remain accurate as projects progress through the delivery cycle

Required Qualifications

2+ years of hands-on GIS production experience supporting utility, pipeline, or engineering projects
Proficiency in ArcGIS Pro: editing, attribution, topology and snapping correction, geoprocessing, data conversion, and export
Working knowledge of the natural gas industry, including distribution system components, terminology, as-built documentation, and service record documentation practices
Experience building and administering Survey123 forms and ArcGIS Field Maps
Experience with ArcGIS Online, including web maps, hosted feature layers, dashboards, and sharing/permissions management
Demonstrated data QA/QC discipline and the ability to catch errors before they reach a client deliverable
Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects at different stages and meet recurring delivery deadlines
Proficiency with Microsoft Teams, Excel, and standard file/server management practices
Clear written communication for client-facing submissions and correction correspondence
Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record

Familiarity with CAD formats and design workflows (DWG/DXF), and coordination with CAD designers

Competencies

Brio Real Estate is a Blackstone Real Estate portfolio company focused on real estate credit. Brio supports Blackstone’s Real Estate Debt Strategies (“BREDS”) investments across the globe. The critical infrastructure and capabilities Brio provides for BREDS allows for effective support in the management of its global portfolio.

Today, BREDS has more than $76 billion of investor capital across high yield / opportunistic real estate credit funds, a publicly traded Mortgage REIT, and liquid securities strategies. BREDS is part of Blackstone Real Estate, the largest owner of commercial real estate globally, owning and operating assets across every major geography and sector.

Role Purpose

At Brio, the Associate, Data Analyst plays a key role in supporting our data ecosystem by connecting technical and business teams and enabling critical day-to-day operations. You will partner with cross-functional stakeholders, including the trading desk, to understand data needs, build queries, and deliver actionable insights. Using platforms like Snowflake, Amazon Redshift, and SQL Server, you will help develop scalable data solutions and support the integration of new datasets into our analytical framework.

Play a central role in our data ecosystem. You'll serve as the critical link connecting technical and business functions, supporting essential workflows that power our daily operations. You'll be instrumental in onboarding and integrating every new dataset that enters our analytical framework.

An experienced data analyst with technical depth. new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Asset Performance Data Analyst working under the Performance Monitoring & Technical Analysis (PMTA) group serves as the regional technical authority responsible for ensuring the performance integrity, reliability, and financial optimization of Standard Solar’s portfolio of solar assets. This role oversees asset performance governance by validating monitoring data, reviewing service tickets and root cause analysis, analyzing production trends, and identifying underperformance, curtailment, and degradation risks.

The Asset Performance Data Analyst plays a key role in protecting asset revenue by performing performance analysis, validating lost energy impacts, and ensuring service actions align with verified technical findings. This position also supports preventative and predictive maintenance strategies by identifying systemic performance issues and recommending operational improvements across assigned regions. Asset Performance Data Analyst ensures monitoring accuracy, service quality, and disciplined performance management across the portfolio while supporting Operational Acceptance (OA), reporting initiatives, and continuous process improvements that strengthen O&M profitability.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Serve as the technical authority for assigned regions, ensuring asset performance integrity, monitoring accuracy, and operational reliability across the solar portfolio.
Review and validate service tickets generated by monitoring partners and contractors to ensure accurate severity classification, root cause identification, and proper documentation of system downtime and performance impacts.
Conduct regular ticket audits to identify data inconsistencies, missing documentation, incorrect categorization, or unresolved operational issues.
Analyze asset performance using measured vs. expected production data, weather-adjusted performance metrics, and trend analysis to identify underperformance, degradation, and operational risks.
Validate curtailment events by coordinating with utilities and reviewing interconnection agreements to confirm event legitimacy, duration, and production impact.
Perform lost energy calculations and validate revenue impact associated with outages, underperformance events, and system degradation.
Support preventative and predictive maintenance strategies by identifying systemic equipment failures, recurring operational issues, and emerging reliability trends.
Collaborate with Vendor Coordination & Management (VCM) to support service dispatch decisions based on validated technical findings and performance analysis.
Ensure data integrity across monitoring platforms, service ticket systems, and reporting tools by validating system configuration, equipment data, and performance records.
Support Operational Acceptance (OA) processes by reviewing asset readiness, confirming ticket resolution, validating monitoring configuration, and recommending technical approval for assets transitioning into O&M operations.
Develop and support performance dashboards, reporting tools, automation initiatives, and data validation frameworks that enhance monitoring accuracy and operational visibility.
identify systemic performance trends and provide recommendations for operational improvements that increase system efficiency, reduce reactive service events, and protect asset revenue.
Support cross-functional collaboration with Engineering, Construction, Asset Management, and third-party monitoring providers to ensure consistent performance governance and scalable O&M operations.
Maintain high ethical and operational standards that promote accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement across the O&M organization.

Supervisory Responsibilities

The Asset Performance Data Analyst does not currently supervise staff but serves as the regional technical authority for ticket validation, asset performance governance, monitoring data integrity, and oversight of third-party monitoring and analysis activities within the O&M framework.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Mathematics, Data Science, Renewable Energy, Economics, or related technical field.
2–5 years of experience in solar asset management, performance analytics, O&M operations, or renewable energy data analysis.
Strong knowledge KPI performance metrics, modeling, and analysis.
Experience with CRM systems.
Proficiency in Excel required; experience with SQL, Python, Power BI, Tableau, or similar reporting tools preferred.
Experience working within Netsuite and/or Salesforce, service ticket platforms, or CMMS systems preferred.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification strongly desired.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex performance data and provide actionable recommendations.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to interface effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Must possess current valid license to drive or otherwise provide transportation if site visits are required.
Must successfully pass background check and pre-employment drug testing.
Must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis for any employer.

Position Routinely Interfaces With

O&M Manager, VP of AM / OPs, and Vendor Coordination & Management (VCM) Team
Third-party Monitoring Providers
Construction & Engineering Departments
Asset Management Team
Senior and Executive Management
Utilities and Interconnection Authorities

Interfaces with customers, vendors, and the public. All employees, including Senior and Executive Management, Sales & Finance.

Physical Demands

Please protect your personal information during any recruitment process. About The Role

We are seeking an experienced, detail-minded data analyst consultant to join our global business development and strategy team. In this role, you will be embedded at Monks, serving as a critical partner dedicated to supporting one of our most prestigious, high-profile client accounts. If you look forward to untangling complex business problems, driving data-led strategy, and thriving in a fast-moving, collaborative environment, we want to hear from you.

Note on Location & Structure:
This is a contract role based out of Austin, Texas, with a hybrid schedule requiring you to be on-site 3 days per week.

About You

The Skills & Toolkit You’ll Bring:

6+ years of experience in a data analyst or analytics consultant role, ideally within a fast-paced agency or global client-facing environment.
Core Tech: Advanced SQL is required; scripting knowledge in Python/Shell is highly preferred.
Data Engine: Strong familiarity with database modeling, data warehousing principles, and using Trino for independent querying.
Data Viz: Experience building dashboards and data visualizations that tell a story (knowledge of Tableau, Superset, and SAP Business Objects is a plus).
Workflow: Complete proficiency in Jira (owning the full ticket lifecycle) and native fluency in Agile/Scrum environments (ceremonies, backlog hygiene, sprint management).

The Mindset We’re Looking For

Insights over Inputs: You don't just pull data; you interpret results, cross-reference data quality, spot the "bad data" anomalies, and surface meaningful strategic insights.
Adaptable & Autonomous: You thrive in a rapid, cross-functional environment, easily self-managing through dynamic priorities and shifting client requirements.
Sharp Communicator: Exceptional presentation and communication skills, with a proven ability to distill complex technical data into clear, actionable narratives for stakeholders at all levels.

The Day-to-Day (Your Impact)

Data Exploration & Architecture

Connect the Dots: Work closely with the team to piece together seemingly disparate data sources, build out robust data pipelines, and create highly interactive, intuitive dashboards.
Deep-Dive Analysis: Immerse yourself in the client's complex financial datasets, applying advanced data discovery and modeling methodologies while collaborating cross-functionally with various data owners and analysts.

Collaboration & Strategy

Bridge the Gap: Partner directly with data product managers and data engineers to translate complex business needs into sharp, actionable analytical requirements.
Influence the Roadmap: Communicate your analysis and strategic insights clearly and effectively to product and leadership teams to directly shape the client’s overarching product strategy.
Proactive Communication: Transparently share and demystify data methodologies and results with a diverse, fast-moving set of global stakeholders.

Benefits

What We Offer

Excellent, full coverage medical, dental, and vision insurance
Generous PTO and 15 company-wide holidays
401k with company contribution
Paid parental leave
Work-life balance with an emphasis on personal well-being
Career growth in a disruptor space & entrepreneurial opportunities within the Monks network
A globally diverse & inclusive culture with employee resource groups such as S4 Melanin, Pride.Monks, Cultura.Monks, and more!
Authentic commitment to DEI efforts and sustainable growth. (Why Sir Martin Sorrell signed The Climate Pledge here!)

This role is subject to our Return to Office (RTO) policy. If you reside within a commutable distance of one of our office locations, you will be expected to work from the office a set number of days per week. The specific details, including the number of required office days, will be in accordance with the company’s then-current RTO policy, which is subject to change from time to time.

Posted Job Title

Job Profile Title

Data Analyst Senior

Job Description Summary

The Senior Data Analyst leads data engineering and data science projects within the lab, turning complex biomedical datasets into robust pipelines, rigorous analyses, and actionable scientific insight. Working closely with the Principal Investigator and research team, this position designs and builds data workflows, develops and applies statistical and machine-learning methods, and ensures the integrity, reproducibility, and quality of the lab's analytical work.

This role requires domain expertise in biomedical informatics, AI/machine learning, or a closely related field, with a focus on immune health and/or high-dimensional omics data (e.g., genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, single-cell, or multi-omics).

This is a senior staff position that operates with significant independence and scientific judgment, and may provide technical mentorship to junior analysts and trainees.

This position is contingent upon continued funding.

Job Responsibilities

Data engineering: design, build, and maintain reproducible data pipelines and workflows for ingesting, cleaning, integrating, and transforming large-scale omics and biomedical datasets.

Project leadership: lead assigned data engineering and data science projects end to end—scoping, planning, and delivering results—while coordinating with the PI and collaborators on priorities and timelines.
Communication & reporting: produce clear analyses, visualizations, and documentation; contribute to manuscripts, grant applications, and presentations; and communicate findings to technical and non-technical audiences.
Rigor, reproducibility & mentorship: uphold standards for code quality, version control, and reproducible research; maintain documentation; and provide technical guidance to junior analysts and trainees.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Biomedical Informatics, Health Information Systems, or Technology Management and 4 to 6 years of experience or equivalent combination of education and experience is required. Master’s degree preferred.

Experience with AWS infrastructure, serverless and containerized SaaS required

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page to understand what drives us and how we work.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Payward's Data team builds and operates the data infrastructure, pipelines, and analytics platforms that power decision-making, reporting, and controls across the business. The team partners closely with functions across the company, including Risk & Audit, IT, Finance, and Engineering, to make sure the data those functions depend on is reliable, well-governed, and ready to stand up to scrutiny.

This role sits within the Data & Audit Readiness team and is dedicated to supporting overall audit readiness from a data standpoint. You will own the inventories, playbooks, catalogs, and access processes that keep the Data team's systems and datasets audit ready, translating audit engagements directly into coordinated, well-documented responses. Because audit readiness is best designed rather than bolted on, this role calls for a data architect's background — someone who has built data pipelines before and knows how to shape them for traceability, access control, and testability from day one. This is a hands-on, builder's role where you will build the ETL pipelines, dashboards, and audit-ready data architecture that let Internal Audit turn audit and review planning into data-driven testing.

The opportunity

Collaborate on the technical coordination and stewardship layer for shared datasets and systems in scope for audit, including financial systems, recordkeeping, and downstream reporting processes.
Spearhead improvements to governance, communication, and coordination around upstream schema and logic changes that impact downstream systems and audit-related processes.
Support technical analysis and downstream impact assessment during the change management process to improve downstream visibility for datasets, tables, and systems in scope for audit.
Support the development and maintenance of reusable audit-ready dataset patterns, including automated validation, data quality checks, and monitoring.
Review processes and datasets in scope for Audit, examine existing operational pain points, and propose reengineering opportunities and longer-term process improvements.
Provide technical guidance to business stakeholders and the Audit PM around specific Audit requests.

What You Bring

7+ years of experience in data analytics or data engineering, ideally supporting internal audit, risk, or SOX compliance functions within the fintech, payments, financial market or crypto where data quality and scale are non-negotiable.
Experience managing and designing data architecture in a regulated environment, having designed and built data pipelines with governance, traceability, and audit requirements considered from the outset.
Hands-on experience building and owning production data pipelines, with strong familiarity with dbt and Airflow or equivalent orchestration tools.
Full mastery of SQL including complex joins, CTEs and analytical functions, alongside strong Python proficiency for pipeline development and analysis.
Experience documenting technical and business requirements, including metadata, KPI definitions, business rules, data process flows, and data dictionaries.
Familiarity with data administration tasks: job scheduling, error/exception handling, and troubleshooting production ETL workflows.
Experience partnering with Data Engineering and/or Data Governance teams on shared datasets, schema changes, and downstream impact analysis.
Strong communicator who can translate audit and business requirements into technical specifications and translate technical work back into terms non-technical stakeholders understand.

Nice to haves

Experience building or scaling a data analytics function within an audit or risk organization from the ground up.
Familiarity with AI-assisted or automation tools for data quality checks, testing, or workflow efficiency.
Familiarity with audit management platforms (e.g., AuditBoard, Jira, Workiva).

Community Summary

Cape Royale is a deed-restricted lakefront community situated approximately five miles from Coldspring in San Jacinto County, Texas. Houston is approximately 65 miles south and is the 5th largest metropolitan center in the United States.

Coldspring is the county seat of San Jacinto County, named for the San Jacinto River which crosses it and in honor of the battle for Texas independence.

Cape Royale sits on the southwest shore of beautiful Lake Livingston. This lake is a reservoir located in the East Texas Piney Woods. Lake Livingston was built and is owned and operated by the Trinity River Authority of Texas under contract with the City of Houston for water-supply purposes.

Role Summary

The Administrative Project Coordinator
plays a vital role in the management of trailer storage oversight, architectural review processes, property compliance, and enforcement of deed restrictions for the community. This position ensures that all construction, renovation, and exterior modification projects meet community guidelines, and that owners remain in compliance with community standards. This individual acts as the primary point of contact for project applications, owner communications, violation processing, and documentation for both the ACC and Deeds Compliance Committees.

Responsibilities

Architectural Control Committee (ACC) Support:

Assist owners with ACC application processes, explain project requirements, and provide ongoing support throughout the review process.
Review incoming project applications, verify documentation, calculate fees, and confirm no outstanding balances on owner accounts before submission to the ACC.
Issue permits and maintain all related documentation in Google Sheets, Cape Files, and CiraNet.
Attend bi-monthly ACC meetings and assist in preparing agendas, meeting minutes, and project summaries.
Serve as liaison between the ACC Committee and property owners regarding application requirements, procedures, and approvals/denials.
Generate and send approval or denial letters with required supporting documents.
Maintain a master ACC Projects spreadsheet and Fee tracking sheet; update weekly.
Prepare permits, track project start/dry-in/end dates, and enforce proper permit display.
Monitor active projects, communicate with owners regarding progress, and coordinate final inspections.
Handle project complaints and ensure timely ACC involvement.
Process final project documentation and oversee refund coordination for deposits.
Track permanent variances and notify owners of filing responsibilities at the County Clerk’s office.

Deed Restriction Compliance

Collaborate with the Deeds Compliance Committee to enforce community standards and restrictions.
Attend monthly Deeds Committee meetings; assist in agenda and minutes preparation.
Issue violation notices, pre-fine notices, and fine letters following owner communication by phone and email/mail.
Maintain the Deeds Violation spreadsheet and update with notes, status changes, and photos.
Escalate unresolved violations in a timely manner and coordinate with the appropriate Committee member or Community Manager.
Ensure fines are accurately added to owner accounts weekly.
Close resolved violations and maintain proper documentation in Cape Files and CiraNet.
Coordinate ACC involvement for violations requiring approval prior to corrective action.
Manage approval of temporary variances as needed (e.g., RV/camper parking).

Administrative & Owner Communication

Maintain accurate digital filing systems across Cape Files and CiraNet for all ACC and Deeds-related documents.
Ensure consistent owner communication and follow-up via phone and CiraMail (for documentation).
Create and manage tasks in CiraNet to track the lifecycle of applications, violations, and projects.

Trailer Storage Management

Assign trailer slips, process lease agreements, and maintain accurate records in the trailer storage spreadsheet.
Add applicable trailer storage fees to owner accounts.

911 Addressing

Maintain and update the 911 Address spreadsheet based on owner submissions and major project applications.
Coordinate with Accounting/AR for address changes and ensure legal descriptions and occupancy status are accurate.
